neighbours.label: emergency containment and hazard-response actions (the area would have to be evacuated, identifying and containing the product, sealing off the zone), as against the same procedural sentences about everyday tasks
fire: If the chemical spill reaches the drains, the whole street may have to be evacuated.
Staff should seal off the ward and isolate any patient showing symptoms.
The response plan covers locating, isolating and removing the infected servers.
In a radiation alarm, the lab must be cleared and the doors locked at once.
Crews worked to contain the oil slick before it reached the beach.
Should the fire spread, the tunnel would need to be closed and ventilated.
The farm was quarantined and all the infected birds were destroyed.
Teams began cordoning off the area and decontaminating the vehicles.
quiet: If the rain reaches the drains, the whole street may have to be swept.
Staff should tidy the ward and greet any patient arriving for a visit.
The holiday plan covers booking, packing and driving to the coast.
At closing time, the lab must be tidied and the lights turned off.
Crews worked to finish the new pier before the summer season.
Should the guests stay late, the hall would need to be cleaned and locked.
The farm was sold and all the chickens went to a neighbour.
Teams began painting the fence and washing the vehicles.
